subtitle: Dump the textures, sounds and models from Minecraft Dungeons II, straight from the game!
description:
Textures are saved as PNGs, or as EXRs for HDR textures, with normal maps rebuilt properly. Sounds and music are saved as OGG files with their original names. Models and animations are saved as GLB files with their skeletons, and when you dump textures at the same time the models use them. Textures and models from your other installed mods are included too.

Dumping sounds, and linking textures to models, needs Native Loader. Without it, textures and models still dump.

Models only use each material's main texture, so effects the game adds in its shaders, like glowing or recoloured parts, are not included.

How to use

Open the game's settings, go to the Mods tab and open Asset Dumper. Turn on what you want to dump, then press Dump. Each type shows a progress bar with roughly how long is left and how big it will be.

You can leave the page and carry on playing while it runs, and it keeps going through loading screens. Cancel Dump stops it, and Continue Dump picks up where it left off, as long as the toggles have not changed. When it finishes, press Open Folder to see the files.

Each dump is saved into its own dated folder in the Dump folder inside this mod's folder, laid out the same way as the game's files.

Requirements

  • Blueprint Loader, which loads this mod

Install

  1. Close the game, and fully close the Minecraft Launcher if you use it.
  2. Open your Minecraft Dungeons II Paks folder.
    • Steam: Right click the game in your library, then Manage > Browse local files, then open Dungeons\Content\Paks
    • Minecraft Launcher: C:\XboxGames\Minecraft Dungeons II\Content\Dungeons\Content\Paks
    If you picked a different install folder in the Minecraft Launcher, it is Minecraft Dungeons II\Content\Dungeons\Content\Paks inside that folder.
  3. Create a folder called ~mods inside the Paks folder if there is not one already.
  4. Open the zip and move the AssetDumper folder inside it into ~mods, so the files end up like this: Paks\~mods\AssetDumper\AssetDumper_P.pak

Uninstall

Delete the AssetDumper folder from ~mods.
